questions.prompt: What is the default maxmemory-policy, and what does it do when memory is full?

options.text: allkeys-lru — it evicts the least-recently-used key
noeviction — it rejects new writes with an OOM error (reads still work)
volatile-ttl — it evicts the soonest-to-expire key
allkeys-random — it evicts a random key

questions.explanation: The default is noeviction: Redis would rather reject writes than delete data. That's safe for a datastore but usually wrong for a cache.

questions.prompt: How do allkeys-* policies differ from volatile-* policies?

options.text: allkeys-* only evict keys with a TTL; volatile-* evict any key
allkeys-* can evict any key; volatile-* only evict keys that have a TTL
They are identical
volatile-* never evict anything

questions.explanation: allkeys-* consider the whole keyspace; volatile-* consider only keys with a TTL set (and fall back to noeviction behavior if none are eligible).

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: maxmemory 0 means no limit
LRU and LFU are approximated by sampling, not tracked exactly
Eviction can remove keys that have no TTL (under an allkeys-* policy)
Eviction and expiration are the same mechanism

questions.explanation: maxmemory 0 is unlimited, LRU/LFU are sampled approximations, and allkeys-* eviction can remove TTL-less keys. Eviction (memory pressure) is DISTINCT from expiration (per-key TTL).

questions.prompt: You set maxmemory-policy volatile-lru but never set TTLs on your keys. What happens when memory fills up?

options.text: Redis evicts random keys anyway
Redis has no eligible keys to evict, so it behaves like noeviction and rejects writes
Redis automatically adds TTLs to all keys
Redis doubles its memory limit

questions.explanation: volatile-* policies only evict keys that have a TTL. With no TTL'd keys, there's nothing to evict, so writes start failing with OOM — like noeviction.

questions.prompt: The configuration directive that sets the maximum memory Redis uses for data is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: maxmemory sets the ceiling (e.g. maxmemory 512mb); 0 means unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why are Redis's LRU and LFU described as approximate?

options.text: They guess randomly
Redis samples a few keys and evicts the best candidate rather than tracking exact usage order for every key
They only work in Redis Cluster
They ignore access patterns entirely

questions.explanation: Tracking perfect LRU/LFU for every key would cost too much, so Redis samples a small set (maxmemory-samples) and evicts the best candidate — a close approximation you can tune.
